correctness.rationale: Strict convexity of Euclidean distance forces every maximizing pair to consist of vertices, so finitely many ordered diametral pairs localize the endpoint. Squared-distance D-bound shows the outward axial linear functionals are strictly positive on nonzero vertex-tangent-cone directions; this makes the axial caps compact and permits a uniform local blow-up. The limiting event a+b<1 over two d-cones has volume (d!)^2 H_v H_w/(2d)!, and normalization by volume(P)^2 gives C(P) epsilon^(2d)+o. Simplicial cone determinants give simplex H_v=2^(d−1)V and the orthotope cap formula, hence C_simplex=d(d+1)4^(d−1)/binom(2d,d) and C_cube=2^d d^(2d)/(2d)!. Independent rational evaluations confirm ratios 32/27 at d3 and 45/64 at d4, with monotonic d2..30; the binomial inequality in the proof handles every d>=2. The statement is for a fixed full-dimensional Euclidean polytope, epsilon down to zero, and ordered pairs.
